text:
A muscle fibre relaxes when calcium ions are actively pumped back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum, removing them from the troponin–tropomyosin complex. This lets tropomyosin block the myosin-binding sites on actin, preventing cross-bridge formation, and the fibre returns to its resting length passively. Neither running out of oxygen nor an overly forceful nerve stimulus causes relaxation—the latter claim is not a real safety mechanism.
CONFIDENCE: 95
